result.question:
There's an open corrective work order on Transformer 1 at site MAIN for the gassing problem, and the crew says the unit has settled down. I want to check that before we close it.

Find the open corrective work order on Transformer 1 that relates to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment. Give me its number, description, priority, failure code and assigned technician. If there's more than one, work with the oldest and list the rest.

Then build two separate findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. Screen hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model. List any flagged timestamps with their values.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the first and the last complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me whether the class stayed the same, moved to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, or got worse.

Decide as follows:
- Close the work order only if both findings say it's calm: nothing is flagged in the last two samples, and the last class is the same as or milder than the first. Put both findings in the resolution notes and keep the existing failure code.
- If exactly one finding points to trouble, don't close it. Add a note saying which check disagreed, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days.
- If both findings point to trouble, keep it open and raise its priority by one level, but not above 1.

Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier. If there's no matching open work order at all, say so, report both findings, and don't create anything.
result.answer:
I left work order 1000052 open and didn't change it. I couldn't produce either finding with the tools you asked for, so the close/hold rule can't be applied yet.

**Work order**
- **Oldest match (the one to act on):** WO **1000052**, "Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check – Transformer 1 thermal fault". It's corrective, status APPR (approved), priority **3**, failure code **FC006** (overheating). No technician is assigned. It was reported 2026-09-30 20:45.
- **Other match:** WO 1000053, "Corrective oil work (oil treatment/degassing/filtration, internal inspection as required)". It's corrective, WAPPR (waiting approval), priority 2, has no failure code and no technician, and was reported 20:47.
- WO 1000051 (tap-changer inspection) is preventive rather than corrective, so I left it out.
- Both matching orders were raised today, two minutes apart. 1000052 is a diagnostic retest, while 1000053 is the actual oil-treatment job. If "the gassing problem" means the oil work, 1000053 is the one you want.

**Samples, 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18:** four daily samples, all complete (all five gases present).

| Timestamp | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 |
| 01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 |
| 01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 |
| 01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 |

**Finding 1 – anomaly screen: not done.**
- There are no anomaly detection models in the model catalog.
- I could have specified a detector directly, but the tool needs the data as a file, and I have no way to write one here.
- Each gas has 4 samples, so your 50%-above-mean fallback doesn't apply. For reference only (not a model result): no sample is more than 50% above its gas's window mean (H2 2873.75, C2H4 16621, C2H2 7 ppm).

**Finding 2 – fault classification: the tool failed.** It returned "LLM unavailable" three times. As a stand-in, I worked out the IEC 60599 gas ratios by hand:
- **First sample (01-15):** C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004, CH4/H2 = 2.60, C2H4/C2H6 = 3.05. That gives code 0-2-2, a thermal fault above 700 °C.
- **Last sample (01-18):** 0.0004, 2.53, 3.05. Same code, same class.
- **Result:** the class stayed the same. One caution: C2H4/C2H6 sits just above 3, the cutoff between the 300–700 °C and above-700 °C classes, so the split is fragile.

**Decision:** Closing needs both findings to be calm. The anomaly screen didn't run and the classification is a manual stand-in, so I didn't close the order. I didn't add the "one check disagreed" note or raise the priority either, because neither finding actually shows trouble.

To finish this, either give me a way to put the samples into a file the anomaly tool can read, or accept the manual results above. Once the classification tool is back up I can rerun it and apply your rule.
